sasha: Heads-up — seeing a perf regression when we enable torch.compile + CUDA graphs for dynamic-length workloads. Repro attached in CI link.

sasha: Baseline (no compile, no cudagraph): p50 ~18ms for seq=512 batch=4. With torch.compile + cudagraph warmup: p50 ~26ms. That's a ~40% regression on tail.

mike: Oof. Do you have kernel traces? sounds like graph capture may be locking in a suboptimal kernel for varied seq lengths.

sasha: Yep. nvprof / Nsight shows we end up running attention_kernel_v1 repeatedly after capture instead of attention_kernel_v2 which is faster for longer seqs. Kernel list sample during run:
```
cutlass_gemm_64x64      12ms
attention_kernel_v1     6ms   <-- chosen after capture
attention_kernel_v2     3ms   <-- better for current shapes
```
So capture seems to pin v1.

elaine: That matches my last experiment: if capture happens at a smaller shape (warmup with short seqs), the cudagraph will reuse those kernels even when inputs expand. For dynamic workloads, capture timing matters.

mike: Two levers: (A) change capture timing (only capture after KV cache priming / stable seq distribution) (B) make the kernel selector aware of "post-capture" re-eval so it can swap kernels even if graph exists. Option B is trickier with CUDA graphs, but we can special-case graph exec to consult selector for kernel affinity.

sasha: Repro snippet we used:
```
# pseudo
inputs = pad_to_max(seq_batch)  # pads to runtime max
# warmup loops with short sequences
for _ in range(5): model(short_inputs)
# now capture
with torch.cuda.graphs.capture(stream):
  out = model(inputs)
```
If warmup uses short_inputs, captured graph binds smaller kernels.

jarrod: We should also inspect KV cache eviction/priming. If KV cache is sparse at capture time, attention tiling choices change. Might explain kernel mismatch.

elaine: I ran an ad-hoc profiler: compile w/o cudagraph = p50 20ms, compile + cudagraph = p50 26ms. nvprof shows ~30–40% more small memcpy ops during capture phase, plus binds to the older kernel variant.

mike: Quick experiments to try:
- force static shapes during capture (pad to fixed multiple) so graph picks the intended kernels
- avoid cudagraph capture if seq variance > threshold
- add small runtime check after capture: if observed dispatch latency >> expected, invalidate graph and re-capture

sasha: I like making capture conditional. For now, plan:
1) disable cudagraph for dynamic workloads by default
2) add per-seqlen kernel affinity in selector (map seq_bucket -> preferred kernel)
3) add telemetry: log kernel id + seq_bucket + compile/cudagraph flag to perf pipeline

mike: I'll own (2). Quick pseudo for selector bias:
```
# in runtime selector
if seq_stddev > 32:
  prefer_low_latency_kernels()
else:
  prefer_high_throughput_kernels()
```
We can choose kernel preference using recent latency histogram per (model, device, seq_bucket).

jarrod: I'll add telemetry counters and a dashboard so we can alert when capture->kernel mismatch occurs. Patch will add: kernel_id, seq_bucket, compile_enabled, cudagraph_enabled as tags to perf events.

elaine: Also a small patch I tried: delaying graph capture until after 2 KV-cache priming requests reduced regression by half. So priming looks effective. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: perf job finished: https://ci.redwood/infer/perf/1749954321 — captured artifacts: traces, nvprof.csv, kernel_choices.log

sasha: Thanks — next steps: mike implement selector changes, jarrod telemetry + dashboard, I'll open an RFC to disable cudagraph by default for dynamic-shape LLMs and include priming recommendations. cc @ops for rollout plan.

mike: I'll post a WIP PR by EOD.

elaine: Nice. If anyone needs my perf traces or the nvprof logs I attached to the CI job, ping me.

sasha: Perfect. Filing RFC + tracking issue now. :white_check_mark:
